overview.title: 📖 Overview: Automatic Sanctity and Fractional Counts
overview.subtitle: Bekhorot 59a–59b
overview.hebrewSource: אָמַר רָבָא: עֲשִׂירִי מֵאֵלָיו הוּא קָדוֹשׁ
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: Rava rules that the tenth animal becomes sanctified automatically once nine have emerged from the pen, even if the owner never explicitly calls it 'the tenth' or it remains inside. The Gemara works hard to locate Rava's actual source, testing and rejecting several baraitot before settling on a case where the ninth was mistakenly called 'tenth' and the true tenth died while still in the pen. Rava's companion principle — that 'a count fit to reach ten' exempts the counted animals even if the count is ultimately never completed — undergoes the same rigorous sourcing process. The daf closes with detailed baraitot working through complex scenarios: fourteen or nineteen lambs emerging through two different pen openings, and why one may never pre-select ten animals for tithing without actually running them through the counting process.

slides.title: 🔟 Does the Tenth Need to Be Named?
slides.subtitle: Rava's claim and the Gemara's four attempts to source it

lines.speaker: Rava
lines.text: The tenth animal is sanctified of its own accord — even if it stays in the pen and is never explicitly called 'tenth.'

lines.speaker: Attempt 1
lines.text: From the baraita: 'the tenth shall be sacred... in any case' — even unnamed. Rejected: maybe it means he called it 'sacred' just not by the specific word 'tenth.'

lines.speaker: Attempt 2 & 3
lines.text: From cases where the owner mistakenly called the ninth 'tenth' and stayed silent, or the ninth 'tenth' and the true tenth then died. Both rejected as distinguishable — perhaps selection or death changes things.

lines.speaker: Final source
lines.text: A baraita: ninth called 'tenth,' and the true tenth simply REMAINS in the pen — the ninth is eaten only with a blemish, and the TENTH IS TITHE. This works even without ever leaving or being named.

slides.title: 🧩 A Contradiction and Its Resolution
slides.subtitle: Whose opinion is really being cited?
rows: Ninth called 'tenth,' true tenth stays in pen → tenth animal has full tithe status
Attributed to Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda's minority view
In the same scenario, the ninth animal is entirely non-sacred
Reconciled: R' Shimon ben Yehuda requires the NAME 'tenth' to be actively removed from the true tenth before the ninth gets any sanctity at all
If an 11th needs 'tenth' removed from the true 10th to become sacred, shouldn't the 9th need the same?
Rejected — an 11th gets the MORE severe sanctity (fit for sacrifice); the 9th's lesser sanctity (blemish-only) doesn't need that same threshold

slides.title: 📊 'A Count Fit to Reach Ten' Exempts
slides.subtitle: Rava's second principle, and its eventual textual source

nodes.content: ❓ Where does Rava's rule come from — that animals counted as part of a group that COULD have reached ten are exempt, even if the count never finishes?
🚫 Attempt: from the mishna where a counted animal jumps back into the pen, exempting all — but maybe that's because the tenth ALSO came out and was tithed on their behalf
🚫 That's ruled out by the mishna's own wording distinguishing 'counted' animals from 'already tithed' animals
✅ Final source: the verse says an animal must be one that WILL 'pass' under the rod — not one that has already effectively passed, i.e., already part of a fit-to-reach-ten count

slides.title: 🚪 Fourteen Lambs, Two Exits
slides.subtitle: Rava's detailed scenarios for the counting procedure

boxes.title: Scenario: 6 + 4, then 4 remain
items: If the last 4 exit through the 6's gate: take one as tithe; the other 4 (from the other gate) combine with a future gathering
If not: the first 6 are exempt (fit-to-ten); the other groups of 4 each combine with future gatherings

boxes.title: Scenario: 4 + 6, then 4 remain
items: If the last 4 exit through the 6's gate: take one as tithe; the first 4 are exempt
If not: the first 4 and the 6 are all exempt (fit-to-ten); the last 4 combine forward

callout.label: Why so detailed:
callout.text: Rava's point: an UNCERTAIN fit-to-ten count (since the remaining animals COULD exit either gate) still exempts — not just a definite one, which he had already stated once.

slides.title: 🐑 No Pre-Selecting Before the Count
slides.subtitle: Why all animals must pass through the pen together

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rava: with fifteen lambs, one may NOT separate out ten in advance, bring only those into the pen, and take one as tithe
2️⃣ Reason (implicit): the count must reflect the animal's true position among ALL the candidates, not an artificially pre-selected subset
3️⃣ Proper method: bring all fifteen into the pen, let ten emerge naturally, and take the tenth as tithe
4️⃣ The remaining five combine with animals born later, for tithing at the next gathering time

summary.principle: The tenth animal's sanctity attaches automatically to its position in a genuine count — it need not be named, and any animal that was part of a count capable of reaching ten is retroactively exempt, but the count itself must be genuine and cannot be artificially pre-arranged.

flowSteps.content: 🔟 Rava: the tenth animal is sacred on its own, even unnamed or left in the pen
🧩 The Gemara tests four baraitot before finding a genuine, unambiguous source

columns.content: 📊 'Count fit to reach ten' exempts, sourced from 'shall PASS' (not already passed)
🚪 Complex two-gate scenarios test whether an uncertain fit-to-ten count still exempts

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: sanctity of the tithe tracks the animal's real numerical position, not the owner's verbal declaration

quiz.q: According to Rava, does the tenth animal need to be explicitly called 'tenth' by its owner to become sanctified as animal tithe?
o: Yes, always — without the declaration it has no sanctity
No — it becomes sacred automatically once it is genuinely the tenth to be counted, even if never named or if it stays in the pen
Only if it is painted red
Only outside Eretz Yisrael
quiz.e: Rava rules that the tenth animal is sanctified 'of its own accord' — its status derives from its actual position in a genuine count, not from a verbal declaration.

quiz.q: In the baraita the Gemara ultimately settles on as the true source for Rava's ruling, what is the scenario?
o: The ninth animal was called 'tenth' and the true tenth animal simply remained in the pen, unnamed
The tenth animal was sold before being named
All ten animals emerged simultaneously
The owner forgot to build a pen
quiz.e: The Gemara's accepted source is a baraita where the owner mistakenly called the ninth animal 'tenth,' and the actual tenth animal stayed in the pen without ever being named — yet it still has full tithe status.

quiz.q: What is Rava's second principle regarding 'a count fit to reach ten' (minyan hara'uy)?
o: Only a definite count of exactly ten animals has any halakhic effect
Animals counted as part of a group that COULD have reached ten are exempt from tithe, even if the full count of ten is ultimately never completed
Ten animals must always be physically present at once
This principle applies only to firstborn animals
quiz.e: Rava teaches that once animals have been counted as part of a sequence capable of reaching ten, they become exempt from any future tithing obligation — even if circumstances (like a death) prevent the count from actually being completed.

quiz.q: What textual source does the Gemara ultimately find for Rava's 'count fit to reach ten' principle?
o: There is no source; it is purely logical
The verse's requirement that an animal 'shall pass' under the rod — implying not one that has, in effect, already passed as part of a fit count
A verse about the paschal offering
A comparison to the laws of teruma
quiz.e: The Gemara derives this from the verse's phrasing that the tenth animal is one that 'will pass' under the rod, excluding an animal that has effectively already passed by virtue of being part of a count capable of reaching ten.

quiz.q: According to Rava, if a person has fifteen lambs, is he permitted to separate ten of them in advance, bring only those into the pen, and take the tenth as tithe?
o: Yes, this is the standard and preferred method
No — he must bring all fifteen into the pen together and let the natural count determine the tenth
Only if he has a rabbi's permission
Only if the lambs are all the same age
quiz.e: Rava rules that one may not pre-select ten lambs in advance; instead, all fifteen must be brought into the pen so that the tenth to emerge naturally through the counting process is designated as tithe.
